# Quarter documentation

> Try Quarter in the simulated sandbox in five minutes, then send provider writes through it, read the state it returns, and react to outcomes.

Quarter runs important writes to the APIs your app depends on, keeps a retry from repeating them, and tells you what happened with evidence. The fastest way to see it is the simulated sandbox: no provider account, five minutes.

## Five-minute quickstart

Log in with a sandbox key, run a Stripe refund, make the next response disappear, run another refund, and watch Quarter prove it happened once. The [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md) explains each step.

terminal:

```bash
quarter login --key qk_test_... --url https://api.example.test
quarter execute --action stripe.refund.create --id refund:order_1042 \
  --input '{"paymentIntent":"pi_test_1042","amount":2500}'
quarter fault stripe timeout_after_commit
quarter execute --action stripe.refund.create --id refund:order_1043 \
  --input '{"paymentIntent":"pi_test_1043","amount":2500}'
quarter events refund:order_1043
quarter effects stripe
quarter proof refund:order_1043 --verify
```

## What Quarter does

Quarter runs important writes to the APIs your app depends on: payments, billing, commerce, CRM, support, email, identity, data and scheduling. 38 providers are supported today, from Stripe and Shopify to HubSpot, Zendesk, Clerk and Supabase. Each write has a stable identity you choose, runs at most once, and ends in a state backed by evidence. When a provider response is lost, Quarter checks the provider and tells you what happened instead of guessing.

- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md): see a lost response resolved in the simulated sandbox.

- [Recipes](/docs/recipes.md): named business actions, such as deleting an account, run as one operation with one signed proof.
- [SDK integrations](/docs/integrations.md): `wrapStripe`, Temporal, Inngest, Trigger.dev, and a Next.js webhook route.
- [Simulated sandbox and test helpers](/docs/sandbox.md): inject provider faults and read what really happened.
- [Idempotency keys](/docs/idempotency.md): safe retries of any request to Quarter's own API.
- [Use Quarter from AI coding tools](/docs/ai-tools.md): the MCP server, `/llms.txt`, and Markdown docs.

- [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks.md): signed deliveries when an action settles.
- [Events and streaming](/docs/events.md): list past events or stream them as they commit.

- [Ledger search and export](/docs/ledger.md): search by metadata, export CSV.

- [Customer-side executor](/docs/executor.md): run provider calls inside your network with your own credentials.

- [Errors](/docs/errors.md): every error code and what to do about it.

## Reference

- [API reference](/docs/api.md): every endpoint, with request and response examples.

- [CLI reference](/docs/cli.md): every `quarter` command and flag.
- [How providers are supported](/docs/providers.md): the three proof paths, and what next and researched mean.

## Conventions

- Examples use `https://api.example.test` as a placeholder base URL. Your early access onboarding gives you the real one. The SDK and the curl examples read it from `QUARTER_API_URL`.
- All request and response bodies are JSON. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.
- Every response carries a `quarter-request-id` header. Include it when you report a problem.
- Action ids can contain `:`. URL-encode them in paths: `refund:order_1042:v1` becomes `refund%3Aorder_1042%3Av1`.

# Quickstart

> Five minutes in the simulated sandbox: run a Stripe refund, lose its response on purpose, and watch Quarter prove it happened once.

This quickstart uses the `quarter` CLI against a simulated sandbox project. It needs no provider account. To send actions from your backend instead, see [Send an action from code](/docs/from-code.md).

## 1. Get a sandbox key and the CLI

Early access teams receive a sandbox project with a `qk_test_` key. The sandbox is simulated: provider calls go to Quarter's provider simulators, so you need no Stripe account and no provider credentials. Build the CLI from the `quarterso/cli` repository. Node 22 or later.

```bash
git clone git@github.com:quarterso/cli.git && cd cli
pnpm install && pnpm build && pnpm link --global
quarter --version
```

## 2. Log in

`quarter login` saves the key and base URL to `~/.quarter/config.json` with mode 0600. `QUARTER_API_KEY` and `QUARTER_API_URL` override it.

```bash
quarter login --key qk_test_... --url https://api.example.test
```

## 3. Run a refund

The id names the business operation. The simulated Stripe applies the refund and answers, and Quarter returns `CONFIRMED` with the refund id in `output.providerObjectId`.

```bash
quarter execute --action stripe.refund.create --id refund:order_1042 \
  --input '{"paymentIntent":"pi_test_1042","amount":2500}'
```

## 4. Lose the next response

`timeout_after_commit` makes the simulated Stripe apply the next write and then never answer. This is the gap where retry code refunds twice.

```bash
quarter fault stripe timeout_after_commit
# { "injected": "timeout_after_commit", "times": 1 }
```

## 5. Run a refund again and watch the timeline

`execute` waits 10 seconds, then returns HTTP 202 with the action still `EXECUTING`. When the dispatch timeout expires, Quarter marks it `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, starts reconciling, and resends the refund with the same Stripe idempotency key. Stripe replays its stored result instead of refunding again, so the action ends `CONFIRMED` with `PROVIDER_NATIVE` assurance. Run `quarter listen` in a second terminal to see the events arrive.

```bash
quarter execute --action stripe.refund.create --id refund:order_1043 \
  --input '{"paymentIntent":"pi_test_1043","amount":2500}'
quarter events refund:order_1043
#   5  ATTEMPT_STARTED            AUTHORIZED -> EXECUTING
#   6  AMBIGUOUS_TRANSPORT        EXECUTING -> OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
#   7  RECONCILIATION_STARTED     OUTCOME_UNKNOWN -> RECONCILING
#   8  RECONCILIATION_STEP        RECONCILING -> RECONCILING
#   9  DETERMINISTIC_CONFIRMED    RECONCILING -> CONFIRMED
```

## 6. Check what the provider really did

`quarter effects stripe` prints the simulator's own record, kept apart from anything Quarter concludes. There is one refund per action: `refund:order_1043` refunded exactly once, although its response was lost.

```bash
quarter effects stripe
# [ { "kind": "refund", "ref": "q_...", "objectId": "re_...", ... },
#   { "kind": "refund", "ref": "q_...", "objectId": "re_...", ... } ]
```

## 7. Verify the proof offline

The Outcome Proof is signed with Ed25519. `--verify` checks the signature against Quarter's published keys on your machine and exits 1 if it does not verify.

```bash
quarter proof refund:order_1043 --verify
# valid: refund:order_1043 is CONFIRMED (PROVIDER_NATIVE), signed by <keyId>
```

## Next steps

- Try the other faults, such as `reset_before_commit` and `lookup_unavailable`: [Simulated sandbox and test helpers](/docs/sandbox.md).
- Send the same refund from TypeScript: [Send an action from code](/docs/from-code.md).
- Send it from Python: [Python SDK](/docs/python-sdk.md).
- Let your coding assistant do this through MCP: [Use Quarter from AI coding tools](/docs/ai-tools.md).
- Every command and flag: [CLI reference](/docs/cli.md).

# Send an action from code

> Install the SDK, send a Stripe refund through Quarter from your backend, and read the state it returns.

This guide sends one Stripe refund through Quarter from TypeScript in a sandbox project. You need Node 22 or later. Using Python? The [Python SDK](/docs/python-sdk.md) has the same calls. To see Quarter handle a lost response first, from the terminal, start with the [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart.md).

## Get an API key

Early access teams receive a sandbox project and its first API key. Sandbox keys start with `qk_test_`; production keys start with `qk_live_`. A key is shown once, when it is created. Quarter stores only a hash. New sandbox projects are [simulated](/docs/sandbox.md): no provider account is needed.

Put the key and the base URL in the environment. The SDK reads both.

```bash
export QUARTER_API_KEY="qk_test_..."
export QUARTER_API_URL="https://api.example.test"
```

> **Note:** Sandbox projects run provider calls against simulators or with test credentials only. A production project refuses any action whose ActionSpec is not certified, with `ACTION_SPEC_NOT_CERTIFIED`. See the [actions reference](/docs/actions.md) for each action's status.

## Install the SDK

Shell:

```bash
pnpm add @quarterso/sdk
```

Python:

```bash
uv add "quarterso[proofs] @ git+ssh://git@github.com/quarterso/sdk-python.git@v0.1.0"
```

TypeScript:

```ts
// quarter.ts
import { Quarter } from "@quarterso/sdk";

export const quarter = new Quarter({ apiKey: process.env.QUARTER_API_KEY! });
```

Python:

```python
import os

from quarter import Quarter

quarter = Quarter(os.environ["QUARTER_API_KEY"])  # base URL from QUARTER_API_URL
```

## Send your first action

An action is one business write. Give it an `id` derived from the business operation, not from the attempt: the refund for order 1042 is always `refund:order_1042:v1`, however many times your code runs. That id is what makes the write happen at most once. See [action identity](/docs/concepts.md#action-identity).

TypeScript:

```ts
import { quarter } from "./quarter";

const action = await quarter.actions.execute({
  id: `refund:${order.id}:v1`,
  action: "stripe.refund.create",
  actor: { type: "service", id: "billing-api" },
  subject: order.id,
  input: {
    paymentIntent: order.paymentIntentId,
    amount: 2500,
    reason: "requested_by_customer",
  },
});

console.log(action.state, action.output?.providerObjectId);
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/actions/execute" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"refund:order_1042:v1","action":"stripe.refund.create","actor":{"type":"service","id":"billing-api"},"subject":"order_1042","input":{"paymentIntent":"pi_3PxExample","amount":2500,"reason":"requested_by_customer"}}'
```

Python:

```python
from quarter import ActionIntent, Actor

action = quarter.actions.execute(
    ActionIntent(
        id=f"refund:{order.id}:v1",
        action="stripe.refund.create",
        actor=Actor(type="service", id="billing-api"),
        subject=order.id,
        input={
            "paymentIntent": order.payment_intent_id,
            "amount": 2500,
            "reason": "requested_by_customer",
        },
    )
)

print(action.state, action.output)
```

`execute` validates the input against the action's ActionSpec, applies your policy, compiles a plan, and dispatches it. In managed mode the request waits up to 10 seconds for the action to settle. You can change the wait with `?wait=<ms>`, up to 30000.

## Read the state

The response is an `ActionView`. When the action settled with a known outcome, the HTTP status is 200. When it is still open, the status is 202 and `state` says why. Neither case is an error.

200 OK:

```json
{
  "actionId": "refund:order_1042:v1",
  "actionType": "stripe.refund.create",
  "provider": "stripe",
  "reason": null,
  "actor": {
    "type": "service",
    "id": "billing-api"
  },
  "subject": "order_1042",
  "metadata": {},
  "fingerprint": "sha256:71394d09cf09f844978ee4429b1a9c6b148f3a78995e27c6363ca79ed0a9471b",
  "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
  "output": {
    "providerObjectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
  },
  "approvalHold": false,
  "proof": {
    "actionId": "refund:order_1042:v1",
    "state": "CONFIRMED",
    "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
    "evidence": [
      {
        "kind": "provider_object_exists",
        "predicate": {
          "type": "provider_object_exists",
          "objectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
        },
        "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
        "verifier": "stripe:dispatch",
        "observedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.912Z",
        "providerObjectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
      }
    ],
    "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
    "compilerVersion": "0.1.0",
    "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
    "verifiedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.915Z"
  },
  "state": "CONFIRMED",
  "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
  "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
  "verdict": {
    "class": "confirmed",
    "retrySafe": false,
    "nextStep": "Nothing to do: the provider applied it.",
    "evidence": {
      "kind": "provider_object_exists",
      "predicate": {
        "type": "provider_object_exists",
        "objectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
      },
      "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
      "verifier": "stripe:dispatch",
      "observedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.912Z",
      "providerObjectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
    }
  },
  "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.915Z"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `state` | Where the action is. Branch on this. See [Handling states](/docs/handling-states.md). |
| `assurance` | How strong the evidence behind the state is. `UNRESOLVED` until a proof exists. |
| `output.providerObjectId` | The provider object the action created or changed, once `CONFIRMED`. |
| `proof` | The Outcome Proof: the evidence, and the spec and plan it was judged against. |
| `fingerprint` | Hash of `action`, `input` and `subject`. The same id with a different fingerprint is refused. |
| `reason` | Short explanation for the current state, when there is one. |

Read the action again at any time, or read its full timeline. Every state change is an event in an append-only ledger.

TypeScript:

```ts
const current = await quarter.actions.get("refund:order_1042:v1");
const timeline = await quarter.actions.events("refund:order_1042:v1");

for (const event of timeline) {
  console.log(event.seq, event.type, event.fromState, "->", event.toState);
}
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/actions/refund%3Aorder_1042%3Av1" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY"

curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/actions/refund%3Aorder_1042%3Av1/events" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY"
```

GET /v1/actions/{actionId}/events:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "seq": 1,
      "type": "INTENT_CREATED",
      "fromState": "CREATED",

        "worker": "api",
        "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
        "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
        "compilerVersion": "0.1.0"
      },
      "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z"

        "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
```

## Send it again

Run the same `execute` call a second time. Quarter returns the existing action and does not call Stripe again. Change `amount` and send it with the same id: Quarter refuses with `ACTION_ID_CONFLICT` (409) before anything is dispatched.

# Python SDK

> Install the Python client, execute an action with the lost-response pattern, and use async, shadow mode, webhook and proof verification, listing and export.

The Python client covers the same API as the TypeScript SDK. It needs Python 3.10 or later and depends only on `httpx`, plus `cryptography` for proof verification. The package is `quarter`, published as the distribution `quarterso`. It has a sync client, `Quarter`, and an async one, `AsyncQuarter`.

## Install

The package is not published to PyPI yet. For now, install it from the private repository over SSH. The `proofs` extra adds `cryptography` for offline proof verification.

```bash
uv add "quarterso[proofs] @ git+ssh://git@github.com/quarterso/sdk-python.git@v0.1.0"
```

The base URL comes from `base_url=`, then from `QUARTER_API_URL`, then defaults to `http://localhost:8080`. The API key is the first argument.

```python
import os

from quarter import Quarter

quarter = Quarter(os.environ["QUARTER_API_KEY"], base_url="https://api.example.test")
```

## Execute an action

Give the `ActionIntent` an `id` derived from the business operation, never from the attempt. `execute` returns an `ActionView`; branch on `state`. It never retries on its own. A 202 is a return value, not an error. See [Handling states](/docs/handling-states.md).

```python
from quarter import ActionIntent, Actor

intent = ActionIntent(
    id=f"refund:{order.id}:v1",
    action="stripe.refund.create",
    actor=Actor(type="service", id="billing-api"),
    subject=f"order:{order.id}",
    input={"paymentIntent": order.payment_intent, "amount": 12900},
)

result = quarter.actions.execute(intent)

if result.state == "CONFIRMED":
    print(result.output)
elif result.state in ("NEEDS_REVIEW", "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"):
    queue_ops_review(result.action_id)
```

### Lost responses

If the response to `execute` is lost, the write may or may not have reached Quarter. The SDK raises `QuarterTransportError` and sets `maybe_executed` to `True` when it cannot rule that out. Resend the same intent: Quarter returns the existing action instead of running it again. Never mint a new id here. See [Idempotency](/docs/idempotency.md).

```python
from quarter import QuarterTransportError

try:
    result = quarter.actions.execute(intent)
except QuarterTransportError as error:
    if not error.maybe_executed:
        raise
    # Same id and input: the server deduplicates.
    result = quarter.actions.execute(intent)
```

GET requests retry up to twice on network errors and 503. Writes retry only when you pass `idempotency_key=`. To wait for a proven outcome, use `execute_and_wait`. It polls until the action settles and raises `QuarterPendingError` when `timeout` (default 60 seconds) runs out.

```python
result = quarter.actions.execute_and_wait(intent, timeout=30.0, poll_interval=0.5)
```

## Async

`AsyncQuarter` has the same surface. Every call is awaited, and lists and `events.stream()` use `async for`.

```python
from quarter import AsyncQuarter

async with AsyncQuarter(api_key, base_url="https://api.example.test") as quarter:
    result = await quarter.actions.execute(intent)

    async for action in quarter.actions.list(state="NEEDS_REVIEW"):
        print(action.action_id)
```

## Shadow mode

`quarter.shadow` runs your own provider call unchanged, returns its result or re-raises its error, and records the observation in the background. Call `flush()` before a short-lived process exits. See [Shadow mode](/docs/shadow-mode.md).

```python
refund = quarter.shadow(
    intent,
    lambda: stripe.Refund.create(**params, idempotency_key=intent.id),
    provider_object_id=lambda r: r.id,
)
quarter.flush()
```

## Verify a webhook

`construct_event` verifies the `quarter-signature` header against the raw body, then parses it. Pass the exact bytes you received, before any JSON parsing. It raises `QuarterSignatureError` on a bad signature or a timestamp more than 300 seconds from your clock. Dedupe by `event.id`. See [Webhooks](/docs/webhooks.md).

```python
from quarter import QuarterSignatureError, construct_event

def handle(raw_body: bytes, headers: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    try:
        event = construct_event(raw_body, headers["quarter-signature"], webhook_secret)
    except QuarterSignatureError:
        return 400
    enqueue(event)
    return 204
```

`quarter.events.stream()` yields events live and resumes with `Last-Event-ID` after a dropped connection.

## Verify a proof

`verify_proof` checks the Ed25519 signature offline against the keys from `proof_keys()` and returns `False` for a bad signature, a changed body, or an unknown `keyId`. Cache the keys. See [Signed proofs](/docs/proofs.md).

```python
from quarter import verify_proof

proof = quarter.actions.proof(action_id)
assert verify_proof(proof, quarter.proof_keys())
```

## List and export

Lists are iterators over every page. Call `.page()` to get one page instead. Filters are keyword arguments: `state`, `provider`, `action_type`, `subject`, `since`, `until` (a string or a `datetime`) and `metadata` (a dict of strings). `limit` sets the page size. `export` takes the same filters and returns the ledger as CSV, without paging.

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=7)

for action in quarter.actions.list(state="NEEDS_REVIEW", provider="stripe", since=since):
    print(action.action_id)

csv_text = quarter.actions.export(
    provider="stripe",
    action_type="stripe.refund.create",
    since=since,
    metadata={"team": "billing"},
)
```

# Concepts

> Action identity and fingerprints, the state machine, reliability classes, evidence and assurance, reconciliation, and Outcome Proof.

Quarter turns a provider write into a sequence: intent, policy, plan, dispatch, evidence, and then either a known outcome or an explicit statement that the outcome is not known yet. This page defines each part.

## Action identity

Every action has an `id` that you choose. It names the business operation, not the HTTP request: `refund:order_1042:v1`, `cancel-subscription:sub_9:2026-09`. Build it from data your system already has, so any process that handles the same operation computes the same id.

- Ids are unique per tenant, up to 255 characters, and can contain `:`.
- Never include a timestamp, a random value or an attempt counter. A new id is a new write.
- The version suffix (`:v1`) is for the rare case where the same business operation must genuinely run again, such as a second partial refund on one order.

Quarter derives the provider idempotency key from the project, the action id and the ActionSpec version pinned when the action was created. The key never changes between attempts. You never send an idempotency key yourself.

### Fingerprints

Quarter hashes the canonical JSON of `action`, `input` and `subject` into `fingerprint` (`sha256:<hex>`). Sending an existing id with the same fingerprint returns the existing action. Sending it with a different fingerprint fails with `ACTION_ID_CONFLICT` (409) and nothing is dispatched. `actor`, `metadata`, `policy` and `deadline` are not part of the fingerprint.

## States

An action is always in exactly one state. Only the ledger changes it, and every change is an append-only event.

| State | Meaning | Final |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATED` | Intent recorded. | No |
| `VALIDATED` | Input matches the ActionSpec schema. | No |
| `AUTHORIZED` | Policy allows it. Waiting for an executor to claim it. | No |
| `EXECUTING` | A provider attempt holds a lease. No second attempt can start. | No |
| `CONFIRMED` | The intended effect exists at the provider. Backed by evidence. | Yes |
| `NOT_EXECUTED` | Proven not to have happened: invalid, denied, or rejected by the provider. | Yes |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` | The attempt may have reached the provider and the response was lost. | No |
| `RECONCILING` | Quarter is asking the provider what happened, within a bounded budget. | No |
| `SAFE_TO_RETRY` | Evidence shows the write did not take effect and another attempt is safe. | No |
| `NEEDS_REVIEW` | Automation cannot decide safely. A person resolves it. | No |
| `COMPENSATING` | A declared compensator is running. | No |
| `COMPENSATED` | The compensator completed. | Yes |

The main transitions: `AUTHORIZED` to `EXECUTING`; from `EXECUTING` to `CONFIRMED`, `NOT_EXECUTED`, `SAFE_TO_RETRY`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` or `NEEDS_REVIEW`; from `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` to `RECONCILING`; from `RECONCILING` to `CONFIRMED`, `NOT_EXECUTED` or `SAFE_TO_RETRY`, or to `NEEDS_REVIEW` when the budget runs out. A policy review sends a new action straight from `VALIDATED` to `NEEDS_REVIEW`.

An executor that crashes mid-attempt loses its lease. The action then becomes `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with reason `LEASE_EXPIRED`, because a crash before dispatch and a crash after dispatch look the same from outside.

## Reliability classes

Each ActionSpec declares what Quarter can guarantee for that action with that provider. The class is a property of the provider's API, not a setting.

| Class | Name | Guarantee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AR0` | Observed | The action is identified and logged. No correctness guarantee. |
| `AR1` | Duplicate-resistant | No concurrent duplicate attempts. An ambiguous attempt is never retried automatically. |
| `AR2` | Retry-safe | Provider-native idempotency absorbs a retry under documented conditions. |
| `AR3` | Reconcilable | After an ambiguous attempt, Quarter determines the outcome from deterministic evidence within a bounded budget. |
| `AR4` | Recoverable | Reconcilable, and a declared compensator exists. No current action is AR4. |

ActionSpecs also carry a status: `experimental`, `preview`, `assured` or `critical`. Production projects accept only `assured` and `critical` specs.

## Evidence and assurance levels

A state that claims an outcome (`CONFIRMED`, `NOT_EXECUTED`, `SAFE_TO_RETRY`) needs typed evidence. Each evidence record names its kind, the predicate it observed, the verifier that produced it, and an assurance level.

| Assurance | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PROVIDER_NATIVE` | The provider's own response or idempotency replay proves the outcome. |
| `DETERMINISTIC_RECONCILIATION` | A deterministic lookup or field comparison proves it. |
| `HEURISTIC_RECONCILIATION` | Suggestive but not conclusive. Recorded on the timeline; never finalizes a state. |
| `MANUAL` | An operator resolved it with an attached, audited note. |
| `UNRESOLVED` | No conclusion yet. |

Which evidence proves what is fixed by the ActionSpec's `evidenceRules`, not by the adapter that collected it. For example, `stripe.refund.create` accepts `provider_object_exists` from dispatch, idempotency replay or a metadata lookup as proof of `CONFIRMED`, but a successful HTTP status alone proves nothing.

## Reconciliation

When an attempt ends ambiguously (timeout, connection reset, 5xx, lost body), the action becomes `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and Quarter opens a reconciliation job. It runs the spec's reconciliation rules in order:

| Rule | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `native_idempotency_replay` | Resends the identical request with the same idempotency key. The provider replays its stored result. |
| `business_key_lookup` | Looks up the object by the action id Quarter wrote into provider metadata. |
| `direct_object_lookup` | Fetches the object by the client id Quarter chose for it. Found proves `CONFIRMED`; absent proves `SAFE_TO_RETRY` when the provider enforces that id as unique. |
| `read_after_write` | Reads the object and compares the fields the action set. |
| `bounded_list_match` | Lists recent objects in a time window and matches them. Heuristic unless the spec says otherwise. |

Each spec sets a `reconciliationBudget`: a maximum number of provider calls, a maximum elapsed time, and a backoff. When the budget runs out without deterministic evidence, the action goes to `NEEDS_REVIEW`. Quarter never retries an ambiguous write it cannot prove safe.

Provider webhooks, when you [configure them](/docs/administration.md#provider-webhooks), are leads: a matching event is recorded as heuristic evidence and starts another reconciliation run. The deterministic lookup, not the webhook, decides the state.

## Outcome Proof

Once an action reaches `CONFIRMED`, `NOT_EXECUTED`, `SAFE_TO_RETRY`, `NEEDS_REVIEW` or `COMPENSATED`, its view carries a `proof`. The proof lists all evidence, the assurance of the evidence that decided the state, and the `specVersion`, `compilerVersion` and `planHash` it was judged against. You can store it next to your own record of the operation.

proof:

```json
{
  "actionId": "refund:order_1042:v1",
  "state": "CONFIRMED",
  "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
  "evidence": [
    {
      "kind": "provider_object_exists",
      "predicate": {
        "type": "provider_object_exists",
        "objectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
      },
      "assurance": "PROVIDER_NATIVE",
      "verifier": "stripe:dispatch",
      "observedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.912Z",
      "providerObjectId": "re_3PxExampleRefund"
    }
  ],
  "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
  "compilerVersion": "0.1.0",
  "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
  "verifiedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.915Z"
}
```

The plan hash identifies the compiled plan exactly. Two actions with the same plan hash were run under the same dedupe strategy, retry rules, reconciliation rules and policy gates.

---

# Handling states

> What your code should do for each state `execute` can return, and for a lost response from Quarter itself.

`execute` returns 200 when the action ended with a known outcome and 202 when it is still open. Uncertainty is data, not an exception: the SDK resolves both, and only errors (4xx) throw. Branch on `state`.

## Summary

| State | HTTP | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFIRMED` | 200 | Done. Store `output.providerObjectId` and, if you keep records, `proof`. |
| `NOT_EXECUTED` | 200 | Nothing happened. Read `reason`, fix the cause, and decide whether this is a new operation. |
| `SAFE_TO_RETRY` | 202 | Call `execute` again with the same intent. |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `RECONCILING` | 202 | Do not retry. Wait for a webhook or poll. |
| `NEEDS_REVIEW` | 202 | Route to a person. Resolve with evidence. |
| `AUTHORIZED`, `EXECUTING` | 202 | Still running. Wait for a webhook or poll. |
| `COMPENSATED` | 200 | The effect was undone by a compensator. Treat as not in effect. |

## A complete handler

refund.ts:

```ts
import { QuarterTransportError, type ActionIntent, type ActionView } from "@quarterso/sdk";
import { quarter } from "./quarter";

export async function refund(intent: ActionIntent): Promise<ActionView> {
  const action = await send(intent);

  switch (action.state) {
    case "CONFIRMED":
      await markRefunded(intent.subject, action.output?.providerObjectId);
      return action;

    case "NOT_EXECUTED":
      await markRefundFailed(intent.subject, action.reason);
      return action;

    case "SAFE_TO_RETRY":
      // Same id, same input: Quarter reuses the idempotency key.
      return send(intent);

    case "NEEDS_REVIEW":
      await openReviewTicket(action.actionId, action.reason);
      return action;

    default:
      // AUTHORIZED, EXECUTING, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, RECONCILING: the webhook finishes the job.
      await markRefundPending(intent.subject, action.actionId);
      return action;
  }
}

async function send(intent: ActionIntent): Promise<ActionView> {
  try {
    return await quarter.actions.execute(intent);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof QuarterTransportError && error.maybeExecuted) {
      return quarter.actions.execute(intent);
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## CONFIRMED

The provider object exists and holds what you asked for. `assurance` says how that was established. Nothing further will change the action unless a compensator runs.

## NOT_EXECUTED

The write did not happen, and there is evidence for that. From `execute`, this is usually a provider rejection (`reason: PROVIDER_REJECTED`), such as a refund larger than the charge. Reconciliation can also end here when a lookup proves absence. Sending the same intent again returns the same `NOT_EXECUTED` action. If you fix the input, it is a different write: give it a new id.

Invalid input and policy denials also end in `NOT_EXECUTED`, but `execute` reports them as errors (`VALIDATION_FAILED` 422, `POLICY_DENIED` 403) with the action view in `error.details.action`. See [Errors](/docs/errors.md).

## SAFE_TO_RETRY

Quarter has proven that the write did not take effect and that another attempt cannot duplicate it. Quarter retries on its own while the spec's retry budget allows (with backoff, and honoring provider rate limit headers after a 429). You receive `SAFE_TO_RETRY` when that budget is used up, or after an operator resolved an action to it. Calling `execute` with the same intent schedules the next attempt with the same idempotency key.

## OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and RECONCILING

The attempt may have reached the provider and the answer was lost. Quarter is finding out. Do not send a new write, and do not treat this as failure. Calling `execute` again is safe but does nothing: Quarter records `RETRY_SUPPRESSED` and returns the same state.

202 Accepted:

```json
{
  "actionId": "refund:order_1042:v1",
  "actionType": "stripe.refund.create",
  "provider": "stripe",
  "reason": "TimeoutError",
  "actor": {
    "type": "service",
    "id": "billing-api"
  },
  "subject": "order_1042",
  "metadata": {},
  "fingerprint": "sha256:71394d09cf09f844978ee4429b1a9c6b148f3a78995e27c6363ca79ed0a9471b",
  "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
  "output": null,
  "approvalHold": false,
  "proof": null,
  "state": "RECONCILING",
  "assurance": "UNRESOLVED",
  "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
  "verdict": {
    "class": "lost_response",
    "retrySafe": false,
    "nextStep": "Do not retry: Quarter is checking with the provider whether it took effect."
  },
  "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:31.402Z"
}
```

Wait for `action.confirmed`, `action.not_executed`, `action.safe_to_retry` or `action.needs_review` on your [webhook](/docs/webhooks.md), or poll `GET /v1/actions/{actionId}` with backoff. For AR3 actions reconciliation usually ends within the spec's `maxElapsedMs` (90 seconds for most).

## NEEDS_REVIEW

Automation cannot decide safely. Either reconciliation ran out of budget, the provider reported success but the object does not match, or a policy rule requires approval. `reason` says which.

202 Accepted:

```json
{
  "actionId": "refund:order_1042:v1",
  "actionType": "stripe.refund.create",
  "provider": "stripe",
  "reason": "amount 2500 above 1000",
  "actor": {
    "type": "service",
    "id": "billing-api"
  },
  "subject": "order_1042",
  "metadata": {},
  "fingerprint": "sha256:71394d09cf09f844978ee4429b1a9c6b148f3a78995e27c6363ca79ed0a9471b",
  "specVersion": "2026-09-29.1",
  "output": null,
  "approvalHold": true,
  "proof": null,
  "state": "NEEDS_REVIEW",
  "assurance": "UNRESOLVED",
  "planHash": "sha256:4e2eae05b83f4e8f50cd3408df3074dc3c7f8a899c1af3c60247f044675e8cbf",
  "verdict": {
    "class": "awaiting_approval",
    "retrySafe": false,
    "nextStep": "A person must approve or reject it. Nothing has been sent."
  },
  "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z"
}
```

A person checks the provider and resolves the action with evidence. Resolutions are audited and never erase the history before them. If a policy held the action before anything was sent (the `action.approval_required` event), use [approve or reject](/docs/api.md#post-v1-actions-actionid-approve) instead.

| Resolution | Use when | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CONFIRMED` | The object exists at the provider. | `evidence.providerObjectId` |
| `NOT_EXECUTED` | The write is proven absent and should not happen. | A note saying what proves it |
| `SAFE_TO_RETRY` | The write is absent and should go ahead. Also releases a policy hold, though approve is the direct route. | A note; then call `execute` again |

TypeScript:

```ts
await quarter.actions.resolve("refund:order_1042:v1", {
  resolution: "SAFE_TO_RETRY",
  reason: "Approved by finance, ticket FIN-311",
  evidence: { kind: "approval", note: "Amount checked against the order" },
});

// Dispatches with the original idempotency key.
await quarter.actions.execute(intent);
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/actions/refund%3Aorder_1042%3Av1/resolve" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resolution":"SAFE_TO_RETRY","reason":"Approved by finance, ticket FIN-311","evidence":{"kind":"approval","note":"Amount checked against the order"}}'
```

If a provider lookup was down when reconciliation ran, `POST /v1/actions/{actionId}/reconcile` runs the budget again instead of resolving by hand. It works from `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and from `NEEDS_REVIEW` after a dispatched attempt.

## AUTHORIZED and EXECUTING

The action is queued or running. In managed mode, `execute` waits up to `?wait=` milliseconds (default 10000) before answering, so you see these states only for slow providers. In executor mode `execute` answers immediately, because the customer-side executor claims the work on its own schedule. Wait for the webhook.

## When the response from Quarter is lost

A timeout or reset between your service and Quarter leaves you not knowing whether Quarter accepted the intent. The SDK raises `QuarterTransportError` with `maybeExecuted: true` for a POST in that case, and for a POST answered with a 5xx. It never retries POSTs on its own. Resend the identical intent. Quarter returns the existing action; it does not run it twice. Never mint a new id to recover.

---

# Operations

> Run several protected actions in order as one operation, reverse confirmed steps when a later one fails, and pause for review instead of guessing.

An operation is an ordered list of 1 to 20 steps. Each step is an ordinary protected action with its own id, plan, evidence and proof. The operation only decides what runs next. It is not a distributed transaction: a confirmed write is reversed by a second provider write, never rolled back.

For common business actions, such as refunding an order or deleting an account, a [recipe](/docs/recipes.md) builds the steps for you. A finished operation has one signed [operation proof](/docs/recipes.md#the-operation-proof) that covers every step.

## Create an operation

Give the operation an `id` derived from the business operation, as you would an action id. Step `n` runs as the action `<operationId>:step:<n>`. A step takes `action`, `input`, and optionally `subject` and `metadata`. The actor is set once for all steps.

TypeScript:

```ts
const op = await quarter.operations.create({
  id: `checkout:${order.id}`,
  actor: { type: "service", id: "checkout-api" },
  compensateOnFailure: true,
  steps: [
    { action: "square.payment.create", input: { sourceId, amountMoney: { amount: 2500, currency: "USD" } } },
    { action: "hubspot.contact.upsert", input: { email, properties: { lifecyclestage: "customer" } } },
    { action: "resend.email.send", input: { from: "orders@example.com", to: [email], subject: "Order confirmed" } },
  ],
});

const current = await quarter.operations.get(op.operationId);
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/operations" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"checkout:order_1042","actor":{"type":"service","id":"checkout-api"},"compensateOnFailure":true,"steps":[{"action":"square.payment.create","input":{"sourceId":"cnon_card","amountMoney":{"amount":2500,"currency":"USD"}}},{"action":"hubspot.contact.upsert","input":{"email":"ada@example.com","properties":{"lifecyclestage":"customer"}}},{"action":"resend.email.send","input":{"from":"orders@example.com","to":["ada@example.com"],"subject":"Order 1042 confirmed"}}]}'
```

201 Created:

```json
{
  "operationId": "checkout:order_1042",
  "state": "RUNNING",
  "reason": null,
  "compensateOnFailure": true,
  "steps": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "actionId": "checkout:order_1042:step:0",
      "actionType": "square.payment.create",
      "state": "CONFIRMED",
      "providerObjectId": "sqPayExample1042"
    },
    {
      "index": 1,
      "actionId": "checkout:order_1042:step:1",
      "actionType": "hubspot.contact.upsert",
      "state": "EXECUTING",
      "providerObjectId": null
    },
    {
      "index": 2,
      "actionId": "checkout:order_1042:step:2",
      "actionType": "resend.email.send",
      "state": "PENDING",
      "providerObjectId": null
    }
  ],
  "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:01.137Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-09-29T19:30:02.410Z"
}
```

Each step in the view carries `providerObjectId` once the step is `CONFIRMED`: the id of the object the provider created or changed, taken from the step's evidence. A step that has not confirmed has `null`.

`POST /v1/operations` returns 201 when it creates the operation and 200 when the same id and steps already exist. The same id with different steps is refused with `ACTION_ID_CONFLICT` (409). Every step's `action` must have an active ActionSpec, or the request fails with `ACTION_SPEC_NOT_FOUND` before anything runs. Read the operation with `GET /v1/operations/{operationId}`.

## How steps advance

- A step starts only when every earlier step is `CONFIRMED`.
- A step in `SAFE_TO_RETRY` is submitted again with the same action id. The evidence already proved a second attempt cannot duplicate it.
- A step in `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` or `RECONCILING` holds the operation in `RUNNING` until reconciliation settles it.
- Advancing only reads step states and submits idempotent actions, so a crash or a second worker never runs a step twice.

| Operation state | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `RUNNING` | A step is running or waiting for its outcome. |
| `COMPLETED` | Every step is `CONFIRMED`. |
| `FAILED` | A step is `NOT_EXECUTED` and nothing needed reversing, or `compensateOnFailure` is off. `reason` names the step. |
| `COMPENSATING` | A step failed after earlier steps confirmed. Quarter is reversing them. |
| `COMPENSATED` | Every confirmed step was reversed. |
| `NEEDS_REVIEW` | A step needs a person, or a confirmed step cannot be reversed. |

## Compensation

With `compensateOnFailure: true`, when a step ends `NOT_EXECUTED` after earlier steps confirmed, Quarter reverses the confirmed steps in reverse order. Each reversal is a protected action of its own, run through the compensator the step's ActionSpec declares. For example, `square.payment.create` declares `square.refund.create` with the payment id and amount of the original.

> **Warning:** Few ActionSpecs declare a compensator today. `stripe.customer.create` and `clerk.user.create` declare a delete of the object they created, which is what lets `customer.onboard` undo itself. If a confirmed step has none, the operation moves to `NEEDS_REVIEW` with a reason that names the step, and nothing is reversed automatically. Check for a `compensation` block in the step's ActionSpec (`GET /v1/specs/{provider}/{action}`) before you rely on it. You can also reverse one confirmed action yourself with `quarter.actions.compensate(actionId, reason)`.

## Review pauses

When a step ends `NEEDS_REVIEW`, the operation stops in `NEEDS_REVIEW` and later steps do not start. Resolve the step's action with `POST /v1/actions/{actionId}/resolve`, using the step's action id. The operation then continues from that step: `CONFIRMED` moves on to the next step, `NOT_EXECUTED` fails or compensates, and `SAFE_TO_RETRY` submits the step again.

## Events

Operations emit their own events, delivered through [webhooks](/docs/webhooks.md) and the [event stream](/docs/events.md) like action events. Each step also emits the usual `action.*` events under its step action id.

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `operation.completed` | Every step confirmed. |
| `operation.failed` | A step did not execute and nothing was reversed. |
| `operation.compensated` | Every confirmed step was reversed. |
| `operation.needs_review` | The operation paused for a person. |

operation.needs_review:

```json
{
  "id": "evt_Q2mX8tRk4Vb1nY7c",
  "type": "operation.needs_review",
  "createdAt": "2026-09-29T19:31:12.004Z",
  "data": {
    "operationId": "checkout:order_1042",
    "state": "NEEDS_REVIEW",
    "reason": "step 1 needs review"
  }
}
```

---

# Recipes

> Run a named business action, such as refunding an order or deleting an account, as one operation of protected steps with one signed proof.

A recipe is a named business action, such as `order.refund` or `account.delete`, that runs a fixed list of provider actions as one [operation](/docs/operations.md). You send one input. Quarter checks it, turns it into steps, and runs each step as an ordinary protected action with its own id, evidence and Outcome Proof. A step starts only after the step before it is proven `CONFIRMED`. When the operation ends you get one signed proof that covers every step.

Recipes are fixed and versioned. There are no conditions beyond skipping a step whose input you left out, no loops, and no code of yours inside them. Quarter does not look up provider ids for you: you pass the ids you already hold.

> **Note:** Like every action today, recipe steps run in sandbox projects until their ActionSpecs are certified. The delete actions used by `account.delete`, and the update actions used by `customer.change_email`, are `preview` specs and have not been run in the Provider Lab yet. See the [actions reference](/docs/actions.md).

## The recipes

| Recipe | What it does | Steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`order.refund`](#order-refund) | Refund a Stripe payment, then record it in your database and email the customer, only once the refund is proven. | 3 |
| [`subscription.cancel_and_notify`](#subscription-cancel-and-notify) | Cancel a Stripe subscription, then record it in your database and email the customer, only once the cancellation is proven. | 3 |
| [`account.delete`](#account-delete) | Close a user's account across your stack: stop billing, then delete them from each provider you name, and remove your own row last. | 6 |
| [`customer.onboard`](#customer-onboard) | Create a Stripe customer and a Clerk user, then write your own row with their ids in stripe_customer_id and clerk_user_id. | 3 |
| [`customer.change_email`](#customer-change-email) | Change a customer's email everywhere you name. | 4 |

### `order.refund`

Refund a Stripe payment, then record it in your database and email the customer, only once the refund is proven.

1. [`stripe.refund.create`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-refund-create): create a refund.
2. [`supabase.row.upsert`](/docs/actions.md#supabase-row-upsert): upsert a row.
3. [`resend.email.send`](/docs/actions.md#resend-email-send): send an email. Runs only when `email` is in the input.

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paymentIntent` | string | Yes |  |
| `amount` | integer | No |  |
| `reason` | string | No |  |
| `record` | object | Yes | A supabase.row.upsert input: table, onConflict and row. |
| `email` | object | No | A resend.email.send input. Omit to skip the email. |

### `subscription.cancel_and_notify`

Cancel a Stripe subscription, then record it in your database and email the customer, only once the cancellation is proven.

1. [`stripe.subscription.cancel`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-subscription-cancel): cancel a subscription.
2. [`supabase.row.upsert`](/docs/actions.md#supabase-row-upsert): upsert a row.
3. [`resend.email.send`](/docs/actions.md#resend-email-send): send an email. Runs only when `email` is in the input.

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subscription` | string | Yes |  |
| `prorate` | boolean | No |  |
| `invoiceNow` | boolean | No |  |
| `record` | object | Yes | A supabase.row.upsert input: table, onConflict and row. |
| `email` | object | No | A resend.email.send input. Omit to skip the email. |

### `account.delete`

Close a user's account across your stack: stop billing, then delete them from each provider you name, and remove your own row last. Every delete is proven by a read that finds the record gone. Deletes cannot be undone, so a failed step stops the run for review.

1. [`stripe.subscription.cancel`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-subscription-cancel): cancel a subscription. Runs only when `stripe.subscription` is in the input.
2. [`stripe.customer.delete`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-customer-delete): delete a customer. Runs only when `stripe` is in the input.
3. [`clerk.user.delete`](/docs/actions.md#clerk-user-delete): delete a user. Runs only when `clerk` is in the input.
4. [`resend.contact.delete`](/docs/actions.md#resend-contact-delete): delete a contact. Runs only when `resend` is in the input.
5. [`hubspot.contact.delete`](/docs/actions.md#hubspot-contact-delete): delete a contact. Runs only when `hubspot` is in the input.
6. [`supabase.row.delete`](/docs/actions.md#supabase-row-delete): delete a row. Runs only when `supabase` is in the input.

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stripe` | object | No |  |
| `stripe.customer` | string | Yes |  |
| `stripe.subscription` | string | No |  |
| `clerk` | object | No |  |
| `clerk.userId` | string | Yes |  |
| `resend` | object | No |  |
| `resend.contact` | string | Yes |  |
| `hubspot` | object | No |  |
| `hubspot.contactId` | string | Yes |  |
| `supabase` | object | No |  |
| `supabase.table` | string | Yes |  |
| `supabase.column` | string | Yes |  |
| `supabase.value` | string or number | Yes |  |

### `customer.onboard`

Create a Stripe customer and a Clerk user, then write your own row with their ids in stripe_customer_id and clerk_user_id. If a later step fails, the customer and user are deleted again, newest first.

1. [`stripe.customer.create`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-customer-create): create a customer.
2. [`clerk.user.create`](/docs/actions.md#clerk-user-create): create a user.
3. [`supabase.row.upsert`](/docs/actions.md#supabase-row-upsert): upsert a row.

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Yes |  |
| `name` | string | No |  |
| `firstName` | string | No |  |
| `lastName` | string | No |  |
| `record` | object | Yes |  |
| `record.table` | string | Yes |  |
| `record.onConflict` | string | Yes |  |
| `record.row` | object | Yes |  |

### `customer.change_email`

Change a customer's email everywhere you name. Clerk goes first and only switches to an address the user has already verified, so an unverified change stops before anything else moves. Every update is by id, so no provider gains a second record. Resend cannot change a contact's email and is not included.

1. [`clerk.user.update`](/docs/actions.md#clerk-user-update): update a user. Runs only when `clerk` is in the input.
2. [`stripe.customer.update`](/docs/actions.md#stripe-customer-update): update a customer. Runs only when `stripe` is in the input.
3. [`hubspot.contact.update`](/docs/actions.md#hubspot-contact-update): update a contact. Runs only when `hubspot` is in the input.
4. [`supabase.row.upsert`](/docs/actions.md#supabase-row-upsert): upsert a row. Runs only when `record` is in the input.

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | Yes |  |
| `clerk` | object | No |  |
| `clerk.userId` | string | Yes |  |
| `clerk.primaryEmailAddressId` | string | Yes |  |
| `stripe` | object | No |  |
| `stripe.customer` | string | Yes |  |
| `hubspot` | object | No |  |
| `hubspot.contactId` | string | Yes |  |
| `record` | object | No | A supabase.row.upsert input that sets the new email on your own row. |

## The recipe format

A recipe is a JSON file of steps. A step's `input` is a literal, or a string that starts with `$.` and reads a path from the recipe input, such as `"$.email"`. Two more forms let a step use what an earlier step made:

- `"$steps.N.providerObjectId"` is the id of the object step `N` created, for example the Stripe customer id. It is filled in when that step is `CONFIRMED`, from the step's recorded evidence. It is the only value a step can read from an earlier step, and step `N` cannot be one that may be skipped.
- A `"..."` key spreads an object from the input into a literal one, so a recipe can add fields to a row you supply. Keys written after it win.

```json
{
  "action": "supabase.row.upsert",
  "input": {
    "table": "$.record.table",
    "onConflict": "$.record.onConflict",
    "row": {
      "...": "$.record.row",
      "stripe_customer_id": "$steps.0.providerObjectId",
      "clerk_user_id": "$steps.1.providerObjectId"
    }
  }
}
```

## Run a recipe

`POST /v1/recipes/{name}/run` (auth: API key)

The body takes an `id`, an `actor` and the recipe's `input`. Derive the `id` from the business action, as you would an action id, for example `delete-account:<userId>:v1`. Step `n` runs as the action `<id>:step:<n>`, counting only the steps that run.

TypeScript:

```ts
const run = await quarter.recipes.run("account.delete", {
  id: `delete-account:${user.id}:v1`,
  actor: { type: "service", id: "accounts-api" },
  input: {
    stripe: { customer: user.stripeCustomerId, subscription: user.stripeSubscriptionId },
    clerk: { userId: user.clerkId },
    resend: { contact: user.email },
    hubspot: { contactId: user.hubspotId },
    supabase: { table: "accounts", column: "id", value: user.id },
  },
});

const current = await quarter.operations.get(run.operationId);
```

Python:

```python
from quarter import Actor

run = quarter.recipes.run(
    "account.delete",
    id=f"delete-account:{user.id}:v1",
    actor=Actor(type="service", id="accounts-api"),
    input={
        "stripe": {"customer": user.stripe_customer_id, "subscription": user.stripe_subscription_id},
        "clerk": {"userId": user.clerk_id},
        "resend": {"contact": user.email},
        "hubspot": {"contactId": user.hubspot_id},
        "supabase": {"table": "accounts", "column": "id", "value": user.id},
    },
)

current = quarter.operations.get(run.operation_id)
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/recipes/account.delete/run" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"delete-account:user_1042:v1","actor":{"type":"service","id":"accounts-api"},"input":{"stripe":{"customer":"cus_QxExample","subscription":"sub_1QxExample"},"clerk":{"userId":"user_2NfExample"},"resend":{"contact":"ada@example.com"},"hubspot":{"contactId":"51"},"supabase":{"table":"accounts","column":"id","value":"acc_1042"}}}'
```

201 Created:


The response is the operation view plus `recipe`, the `name@version` that ran. Follow it with `GET /v1/operations/{operationId}`, or with the `operation.*` [events](/docs/events.md). Each step also emits the usual `action.*` events under its step action id.

### Onboard and change email

`customer.onboard` takes the customer's `email`, optional names, and a `record` that names your table, its `onConflict` column and the `row` to write. `customer.change_email` takes the new `email` and one block per system that holds it. Send only the blocks you use: a step whose block is missing is skipped.

TypeScript:

```ts
const onboard = await quarter.recipes.run("customer.onboard", {
  id: `onboard:${signup.id}:v1`,
  actor: { type: "service", id: "signup-api" },
  input: {
    email: signup.email,
    name: signup.name,
    firstName: signup.firstName,
    lastName: signup.lastName,
    record: { table: "accounts", onConflict: "id", row: { id: signup.id, email: signup.email } },
  },
});

const change = await quarter.recipes.run("customer.change_email", {
  id: `change-email:${user.id}:v1`,
  actor: { type: "service", id: "accounts-api" },
  input: {
    email: newEmail,
    clerk: { userId: user.clerkId, primaryEmailAddressId: verifiedAddressId },
    stripe: { customer: user.stripeCustomerId },
    hubspot: { contactId: user.hubspotId },
    record: { table: "accounts", onConflict: "id", row: { id: user.id, email: newEmail } },
  },
});
```

Python:

```python
onboard = quarter.recipes.run(
    "customer.onboard",
    id=f"onboard:{signup.id}:v1",
    actor=Actor(type="service", id="signup-api"),
    input={
        "email": signup.email,
        "name": signup.name,
        "firstName": signup.first_name,
        "lastName": signup.last_name,
        "record": {"table": "accounts", "onConflict": "id", "row": {"id": signup.id, "email": signup.email}},
    },
)

change = quarter.recipes.run(
    "customer.change_email",
    id=f"change-email:{user.id}:v1",
    actor=Actor(type="service", id="accounts-api"),
    input={
        "email": new_email,
        "clerk": {"userId": user.clerk_id, "primaryEmailAddressId": verified_address_id},
        "stripe": {"customer": user.stripe_customer_id},
        "hubspot": {"contactId": user.hubspot_id},
        "record": {"table": "accounts", "onConflict": "id", "row": {"id": user.id, "email": new_email}},
    },
)
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/recipes/customer.onboard/run" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"onboard:signup_1042:v1","actor":{"type":"service","id":"signup-api"},"input":{"email":"ada@example.com","name":"Ada Lovelace","firstName":"Ada","lastName":"Lovelace","record":{"table":"accounts","onConflict":"id","row":{"id":"signup_1042","email":"ada@example.com"}}}}'

curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/recipes/customer.change_email/run" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"id":"change-email:user_1042:v1","actor":{"type":"service","id":"accounts-api"},"input":{"email":"ada@newmail.example","clerk":{"userId":"user_2NfExample","primaryEmailAddressId":"idn_2NfExample"},"stripe":{"customer":"cus_QxExample"},"hubspot":{"contactId":"51"},"record":{"table":"accounts","onConflict":"id","row":{"id":"acc_1042","email":"ada@newmail.example"}}}}'
```

## List and describe recipes

`GET /v1/recipes` (auth: API key)

`GET /v1/recipes/{name}` (auth: API key)

Both return each recipe's `name`, `version`, `summary`, `compensateOnFailure`, its `steps` as `{ action, optional }`, and its `inputSchema` as JSON Schema. An unknown name returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (404).

TypeScript:

```ts
const all = await quarter.recipes.list();
const recipe = await quarter.recipes.get("account.delete");
```

curl:

```bash
curl "$QUARTER_API_URL/v1/recipes/account.delete" \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $QUARTER_API_KEY"
```

## Idempotency

- The same `id` never runs twice. Sending the same `id` and input again returns the existing operation with 200 instead of 201, whatever state it is in.
- The same `id` with a different input is refused with `ACTION_ID_CONFLICT` (409) and runs nothing.
- Recipe ids and operation ids share one namespace in a project. Use a prefix per recipe.
- A corrected input is a new business action: give it a new `id`, such as `:v2`.

## When the input does not fit

Quarter checks the input against the recipe's `inputSchema`, then checks every step's input against that step's ActionSpec, before anything runs. A mismatch returns `VALIDATION_FAILED` (422). `details.errors` lists each problem, and a step problem names the recipe step and its action. Nothing is created, so fix the input and send it again with the same `id`.

422 Unprocessable Entity:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
    "message": "input does not fit account.delete",
    "details": {
      "errors": [
        "step 2 (clerk.user.delete) /userId must match pattern \"^user_\""
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## When a step fails

`account.delete`, `order.refund`, `subscription.cancel_and_notify` and `customer.change_email` run with `compensateOnFailure: false`. When a step cannot be proven, the operation stops and later steps do not start. Nothing that already happened is undone. `customer.onboard` runs with `compensateOnFailure: true`, described [below](#what-customer-onboard-proves).

| Step outcome | Operation | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NOT_EXECUTED`, for example a provider rejection | `FAILED`, with a `reason` such as `step 2 did not execute: ...` | Read the step's action. Fix the cause and run the recipe with a new `id`. |
| `NEEDS_REVIEW`, or the step used its retry budget | `NEEDS_REVIEW`, with a `reason` that names the step | Resolve the step's action with `POST /v1/actions/{actionId}/resolve`. The operation then continues from that step. |
| `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` or `RECONCILING` | `RUNNING` | Wait. Reconciliation settles the step first. |

> **Warning:** Deletes cannot be undone. If a step of `account.delete` fails, the providers before it have already deleted their records. The run stops there so a person can look at it, and it never guesses at the rest.

## The operation proof

`GET /v1/operations/{operationId}/proof` (auth: API key)

Once the operation has finished (`COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `NEEDS_REVIEW` or `COMPENSATED`), Quarter signs one manifest for it. `body.steps` lists each step's action id, action type, state and `proofHash`, the SHA-256 of that step's own [Outcome Proof](/docs/proofs.md) body. A step with no proof yet has no `proofHash`. While the operation is `RUNNING` or `COMPENSATING` the endpoint returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (404).

200 OK:

```json
{
  "body": {
    "kind": "operation",
    "operationId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1",
    "tenantId": "5b1f0c7e-2d4a-4f39-9a51-0c6f1e2b7d10",
    "projectId": "9e3a6d21-84b0-4c7f-b1d2-6f0a3e5c8b47",
    "state": "COMPLETED",
    "reason": null,
    "steps": [
      {
        "index": 0,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:0",
        "actionType": "stripe.subscription.cancel",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:0b8e5f1c2a9d4e7f3b6a1c8d5e2f9a4b7c0d3e6f1a8b5c2d9e4f7a0b3c6d1e8f"
      },
      {
        "index": 1,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:1",
        "actionType": "stripe.customer.delete",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:5d2a8f3e6b1c9d4a7e0f3b8c5a2d9e6f1b4c7a0d3e8f5b2c9a6d1e4f7b0c3a8d"
      },
      {
        "index": 2,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:2",
        "actionType": "clerk.user.delete",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:9c4f1a7e3d0b6c8f2a5e9d1b4c7f0a3e6d9b2c5f8a1e4d7b0c3f6a9e2d5b8c1f"
      },
      {
        "index": 3,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:3",
        "actionType": "resend.contact.delete",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:2e7b4d9a1f6c3e8b5d0a7f2c9e4b1d6a3f8c5e0b7d2a9f4c1e6b3d8a5f0c7e2b"
      },
      {
        "index": 4,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:4",
        "actionType": "hubspot.contact.delete",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:7a1d6f3b8e5c2a9f4d1b6e3c8a5f2d9b4e7c0a3f6d1b8e5c2a7f4d9b6e1c3a8f"
      },
      {
        "index": 5,
        "actionId": "delete-account:user_1042:v1:step:5",
        "actionType": "supabase.row.delete",
        "state": "CONFIRMED",
        "proofHash": "sha256:4f9c2e7a1d6b3f8e5a0c7d2b9f4e1a6c3d8b5f0e7a2c9d4b1f6e3a8c5d0b7e2a"
      }
    ],
    "issuedAt": "2026-09-29T19:40:09.244Z"
  },
  "keyId": "2026-09",
  "signature": "base64url Ed25519 signature"
```
